title: Luke Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 23.

questions.question: In Luke 23, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The multitude led Jesus unto Pilate
Pilate asked if Jesus was the King of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The multitude led Jesus unto Pilate
questions.explanation: The multitude arose and led Jesus unto Pilate, which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: What did the multitude accuse Jesus of in Luke 23?
questions.explanation: The multitude accused Jesus of perverting the nation according to Luke 23:2.

questions.question: What did Pilate say after examining Jesus?
options: I find no fault in this man
questions.correctAnswer: I find no fault in this man
questions.explanation: Pilate stated that he found no fault in Jesus after examining him as noted in Luke 23:4.

questions.question: Who did Pilate send Jesus to after hearing he was from Galilee?
questions.explanation: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod because he belonged to Herod's jurisdiction, as mentioned in Luke 23:7.

questions.question: What was Herod's reaction upon seeing Jesus?
questions.explanation: Herod was exceedingly glad to see Jesus because he had longed to see him, as stated in Luke 23:8.

questions.question: How did Herod treat Jesus during their encounter?
questions.explanation: Herod mocked Jesus and set him at nought, as described in Luke 23:11.

questions.question: What did Pilate find after examining Jesus and sending him to Herod?
questions.explanation: Pilate stated that neither he nor Herod found anything worthy of death in Jesus, as noted in Luke 23:15.

questions.question: What did the chief priests and scribes do while Herod questioned Jesus?
questions.explanation: The chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused Jesus while Herod questioned him, as stated in Luke 23:10.

questions.question: What did the people cry out for Pilate to do?
questions.explanation: The people cried out to release Barabbas instead of Jesus, as indicated in Luke 23:18.

questions.question: What was Barabbas imprisoned for?
questions.explanation: Barabbas was imprisoned for a certain sedition and murder, according to Luke 23:19.

questions.question: Did Pilate and Herod become friends?
questions.explanation: Pilate and Herod were made friends on the same day after their interactions over Jesus, as stated in Luke 23:12.

questions.question: Did Pilate find fault in Jesus according to the text?
questions.explanation: Pilate explicitly states he found no fault in Jesus in Luke 23:4.

questions.question: Was Jesus silent during his questioning by Herod?
questions.explanation: Jesus answered nothing to Herod during questioning, as mentioned in Luke 23:9.

questions.question: The chief priests defended Jesus during the trial.
questions.explanation: The chief priests and scribes vehemently accused Jesus, not defended him, as stated in Luke 23:10.

questions.question: The multitude wanted to release Jesus instead of Barabbas.
questions.explanation: The multitude cried out to release Barabbas, not Jesus, as indicated in Luke 23:18.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Pilate express he was willing to do regarding Jesus?
questions.explanation: Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them. (Luke 23:20)

questions.question: What does Luke 23:21 promise will happen if someone does what Luke 23:20 commands?
questions.explanation: But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. (Luke 23:21)

questions.question: How many times did Pilate ask the crowd about Jesus' evil deeds?
questions.explanation: And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? (Luke 23:22)

questions.question: What was the crowd's response when Pilate sought to release Jesus?
questions.explanation: And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. (Luke 23:23)

questions.question: What did Pilate ultimately decide regarding Jesus?
questions.explanation: And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required. (Luke 23:24)

questions.question: What was the reason for releasing Barabbas instead of Jesus?
options: He was a murderer and seditionist
questions.correctAnswer: He was a murderer and seditionist
questions.explanation: And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison. (Luke 23:25)

questions.question: Who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross?
questions.explanation: And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country. (Luke 23:26)

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the Daughters of Jerusalem?
options: Weep for yourselves and your children
questions.correctAnswer: Weep for yourselves and your children
questions.explanation: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. (Luke 23:28)

questions.question: What did Jesus ask for concerning those who crucified him?
questions.explanation: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. (Luke 23:34)

questions.question: What mockery did the rulers and soldiers make of Jesus?
questions.explanation: And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself. (Luke 23:35)

questions.question: What was written over Jesus in different languages?
options: This is the King of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: This is the King of the Jews
questions.explanation: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS. (Luke 23:38)

questions.question: What does Luke 23:31 imply about the consequences of actions in different circumstances?
questions.explanation: For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? (Luke 23:31)

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus asked the Father to forgive those who were crucifying him?
questions.explanation: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. (Luke 23:34)

questions.question: Is it false that Pilate found fault in Jesus?
questions.explanation: I find no fault in this man. (Luke 23:4)

questions.question: Is it false that the crowd chose to release Barabbas instead of Jesus?
questions.explanation: And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas. (Luke 23:18)

hard.title: Luke Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 23.

questions.question: What did one of the malefactors say to Jesus while being crucified?
options: If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
Remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
Certainly this was a righteous man.
Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.
questions.correctAnswer: If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
questions.explanation: This is found in Luke 23:39, where one of the malefactors railed against Jesus, challenging his identity as Christ.

questions.question: What did the other malefactor say in response to the first malefactor's challenge?
options: We receive the due reward of our deeds.
Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.
questions.explanation: This response is found in Luke 23:40, where the second malefactor rebukes the first for not fearing God.

questions.question: What did the second malefactor acknowledge about their punishment?
options: We receive the due reward of our deeds.
questions.correctAnswer: We receive the due reward of our deeds.
questions.explanation: This statement is found in Luke 23:41, where the malefactor admits their guilt in contrast to Jesus' innocence.

questions.question: What did the second malefactor ask Jesus?
options: Remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
questions.correctAnswer: Remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
questions.explanation: This request is found in Luke 23:42, where the malefactor seeks to be remembered by Jesus.

questions.question: What was Jesus' response to the malefactor's request?
options: To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
questions.correctAnswer: To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
questions.explanation: This promise is found in Luke 23:43, where Jesus assures the malefactor of his salvation.

questions.question: What happened to the sun at the sixth hour?
questions.explanation: This event is recorded in Luke 23:44, indicating a supernatural darkness during the crucifixion.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'paradeisos' in Luke 23:43 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Paradeisos' refers to a place of bliss or a garden, aligning with the concept of paradise mentioned in Luke 23:43.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in the statement 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit'?
questions.explanation: This statement is an apostrophe as Jesus is addressing God directly in a heartfelt manner, found in Luke 23:46.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of unjust suffering in Luke 23:41?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 prophesies the suffering of the Messiah, which parallels the innocent suffering Jesus experienced, as acknowledged in Luke 23:41.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the promise made by Jesus in Luke 23:43?
questions.explanation: Revelation 2:7 speaks of the promise of paradise to those who overcome, fulfilling the promise made in Luke 23:43.

questions.question: What follows the statement 'Certainly this was a righteous man' in Luke 23:47?
options: And the people smote their breasts.
He was taken to the tomb.
questions.correctAnswer: And the people smote their breasts.
questions.explanation: This follows in Luke 23:48, showing the people's reaction to the events at the crucifixion.

questions.question: What literary device is present in Luke 23:45 with the tearing of the temple veil?
questions.explanation: The tearing of the veil symbolizes the new access to God through Jesus' sacrifice, as described in Luke 23:45.

questions.question: Joseph of Arimathaea did not consent to what, according to Luke 23:51?
options: The counsel and deed of them.
questions.correctAnswer: The counsel and deed of them.
questions.explanation: This statement in Luke 23:51 indicates Joseph's dissent from the decisions made by the council regarding Jesus.

questions.question: Jesus' statement 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit' indicates what about his relationship with God?
questions.explanation: This statement in Luke 23:46 reflects Jesus' trust and reliance on God, affirming his relationship with the Father.

questions.question: The women who followed Jesus prepared spices and ointments for his body after his death.
questions.explanation: While the women prepared spices and ointments, they did so before resting on the Sabbath, as indicated in Luke 23:56.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 23:4 teach about Christ's innocence and human sin?
options: Jesus was without fault even though accused by sinful men
Jesus was guilty but forgiven by Pilate
Jesus sinned but was judged unfairly
Jesus was partially responsible for the people's sins
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus was without fault even though accused by sinful men
questions.explanation: Luke 23:4 states, 'I find no fault in this man,' indicating Jesus' innocence despite human accusations, highlighting the doctrine of Christ's sinlessness.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' kingship is revealed in Luke 23:3?
options: Jesus acknowledges His messianic kingship in a way that fulfills prophecy
Jesus denies being a king to avoid conflict
Jesus claims earthly political power over the Jews
Jesus refuses to answer Pilate's question
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus acknowledges His messianic kingship in a way that fulfills prophecy
questions.explanation: Luke 23:3 records Jesus' answer, 'Thou sayest it,' affirming His identity as King of the Jews in a messianic sense, fulfilling Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' submission to human authorities is taught in Luke 23:24?
options: Jesus submits to human judgment despite innocence
Jesus overthrows Pilate to establish His kingdom
Jesus escapes crucifixion through divine intervention
Jesus is judged only by God, not by humans
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus submits to human judgment despite innocence
questions.explanation: Luke 23:24 states Pilate 'gave sentence that it should be as they required,' showing Jesus' willing submission to unjust human authority as part of the redemptive plan.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 23:34 specifically demonstrate when Jesus says, 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do'?
questions.explanation: In Luke 23:34, Jesus' request for forgiveness for His executioners reveals God's attribute of mercy, showing compassion even toward sinners.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God rending the temple veil at Jesus’ death in Luke 23:45?
questions.explanation: Luke 23:45 describes the veil of the temple being torn, symbolizing God's sovereign act in ending the separation between God and man through Christ's death.

questions.question: How does Luke 23:26-31 connect the passion narrative to Old Testament prophetic themes?
options: It fulfills the prophecy of the suffering servant who bears the sins of many
It shows Jesus as a political revolutionary overthrowing Rome
It illustrates Jesus’ rejection of all prophecy
It emphasizes Jesus’ divine nature over his humanity
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophecy of the suffering servant who bears the sins of many
questions.explanation: Verses 26-31 depict Jesus bearing the cross and warning those who mourn, echoing Isaiah's suffering servant who bears sin, linking the passion to prophetic fulfillment.

questions.question: In what way does Luke 23:50-53 prepare for the resurrection narrative in the Gospel?
options: By recounting Joseph of Arimathaea’s burial of Jesus in a new tomb
By describing Jesus’ escape from the tomb
By emphasizing Jesus’ burial by the chief priests
By focusing on Roman guards securing the tomb
questions.correctAnswer: By recounting Joseph of Arimathaea’s burial of Jesus in a new tomb
questions.explanation: Luke 23:50-53 narrates Joseph of Arimathaea’s respectful burial of Jesus in a new tomb, setting the stage for the resurrection account.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 23:43 and Luke 23:46 teach about salvation and Jesus' divine-human nature?
options: Jesus grants immediate salvation while entrusting His spirit to the Father, affirming both divinity and humanity
Jesus delays judgment until after resurrection
Jesus abandons His human spirit at death
Jesus saves only after a period of purgatory
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus grants immediate salvation while entrusting His spirit to the Father, affirming both divinity and humanity
questions.explanation: Luke 23:43 shows Jesus promising paradise to the repentant thief, and 23:46 records Jesus committing His spirit to the Father, affirming His divine authority and true humanity in death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 23:34 and Luke 23:39-43 teach about repentance and divine forgiveness?
options: God’s forgiveness is extended even to sinners at the point of true repentance
Forgiveness requires perfect works before death
Only the innocent can receive forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s forgiveness is extended even to sinners at the point of true repentance
questions.explanation: Luke 23:34 shows Jesus asking forgiveness for His persecutors, while 23:39-43 records the penitent thief receiving salvation, illustrating forgiveness granted upon repentance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human responsibility and divine justice do Luke 23:40-41 and Luke 23:47 teach?
options: Humans receive just reward for deeds, yet divine revelation leads to recognition of righteousness
All people are innocent before God
Human deeds are irrelevant to divine judgment
Only the Jewish leaders are responsible for Jesus’ death
questions.correctAnswer: Humans receive just reward for deeds, yet divine revelation leads to recognition of righteousness
questions.explanation: Luke 23:40-41 affirms just punishment for deeds, while 23:47 shows the centurion glorifying God after witnessing Jesus’ death, highlighting divine justice and revelation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Luke 23:44-46 shows natural phenomena disproving the resurrection story. What does the passage actually teach?
options: The darkness and temple veil rent signify divine judgment and the cosmic significance of Jesus’ death
The darkness was a solar eclipse that proves Jesus died
The phenomena are purely symbolic with no historical basis
The events were natural and unrelated to Jesus’ death
questions.correctAnswer: The darkness and temple veil rent signify divine judgment and the cosmic significance of Jesus’ death
questions.explanation: Luke 23:44-46 describes darkness and the temple veil tearing at Jesus’ death, indicating God's judgment and the breaking of the barrier between God and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 23:17 teach about Jewish customs and Jesus’ legal release?
options: Jesus' release was tied to the Passover custom of releasing a prisoner
Jesus was released according to Roman law without regard to Jewish custom
Jesus was illegally detained without trial
Jesus' release was a purely political act without religious significance
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' release was tied to the Passover custom of releasing a prisoner
questions.explanation: Luke 23:17 notes, 'For of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast,' showing the Jewish custom influencing Pilate's decision.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 23:47 demonstrate when the centurion says, 'Certainly this was a righteous man'?
questions.explanation: Luke 23:47 records the centurion glorifying God upon witnessing Jesus’ death, showing God’s attribute of revelation enabling recognition of righteousness.

questions.question: How does Luke 23:28-30 prepare readers for eschatological judgment themes in Scripture?
options: By warning of coming tribulation and judgment upon Jerusalem and its people
By denying any future judgment for Israel
By focusing solely on Jesus’ death without future implications
questions.correctAnswer: By warning of coming tribulation and judgment upon Jerusalem and its people
questions.explanation: Luke 23:28-30 contains Jesus’ prophetic warning about future suffering and judgment, aligning with eschatological themes found in the prophets.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 23:7 and Luke 23:12 teach about Jesus’ role in reconciling hostile parties?
options: Jesus’ trial leads to temporary reconciliation between Pilate and Herod, symbolizing peace through Him
Jesus establishes a political kingdom immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ trial leads to temporary reconciliation between Pilate and Herod, symbolizing peace through Him
questions.explanation: Luke 23:7-12 narrate Jesus being sent to Herod and the subsequent friendship between Pilate and Herod, symbolizing Jesus’ role in peace-making.
